# HTTP API

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:gen` (scripts/docs/reference.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every route `notesd` serves on `127.0.0.1:7317`. The list comes from the daemon's own route table;
the descriptions live in `scripts/docs/httpRoutes.ts`, and `npm test` fails when a route has none.

## Health and MCP

The daemon listens on `127.0.0.1` only and has no authentication. Three guards recur below. **Same-origin only**: the request must reach a loopback host and carry an `Origin` equal to that host (the wall's own page); anything else, a plain `curl` included, gets 403 `forbidden_origin`. **Loopback only**: the request URL must name a loopback host and an `Origin`, when sent, must be loopback too (403 `forbidden_host` / `forbidden_origin`). **Hook routes** add the header `X-Notes-Capture: 1` and a JSON body to the loopback rule. Errors are JSON `{ "error": "<code>" }`; a body that is not JSON answers 400 `invalid_json`, and a body or query that fails validation answers 400 with the failing fields in `error`. Note, photo and file ids are accepted in any case, with or without the dash; a malformed one answers 400 `invalid_id` unless a row says otherwise.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | `{"ok":true,"service":"notesd"}`. What `scripts/install.sh` waits for. |
| `POST /mcp` | The `notes` MCP server (streamable HTTP, stateless: one JSON-RPC exchange per request). Loopback only: 403 with a JSON-RPC error for another `Host` or a non-loopback `Origin`. The tools are in [mcp-tools.md](mcp-tools.md). |
| `GET /mcp` | 405 `Method not allowed` with `Allow: POST`. The server keeps no standalone event stream. |
| `DELETE /mcp` | 405 `Method not allowed` with `Allow: POST`. There are no MCP sessions to end. |

## Notes

Every note in an answer carries `id`, `body`, `tags`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `origin`, `images` and `files`. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/notes` | Live notes, most recently edited first: `{notes, next_cursor}`. Query: `tag` (repeatable, all must match, `#` optional), `has_image=true\|false`, `limit` (1 to 5000, default 2000), `cursor`. Sends an `ETag`; a matching `If-None-Match` answers 304 after one aggregate query. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id` | One live note. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted one. |
| `POST /api/notes` | `{body}`: a new note with origin `{source: "web"}`. An empty body is allowed (the wall creates the note, then the editor fills it). 201 with the note. |
| `PATCH /api/notes/:id` | `{body}`: replace the body. The old body is kept as a revision in the same transaction. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note. |
| `DELETE /api/notes/:id` | Soft delete: the note goes to the recycle bin. Returns the note. 404 `not_found` when it is not live. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/restore` | Bring a deleted note back. Restoring a live note returns it unchanged. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/tags` | Every tag of the live notes with its count and last use. Sends an `ETag`; 304 on a matching `If-None-Match`. |
| `GET /api/events` | Server-sent events for the wall: `event: note` `{op, id}` on every note change, `event: chat` `{op, thread_id, id}` on every chat change, `event: adversary` `{op, strategy_id, session_date}` on every reviewer change (`op`: `verdict`, `mark`, `toggle`, `run`). A comment line every 25 s keeps it open. Only this daemon's writes appear; the other machine's reach the wall by polling. |

## Recycle bin

Soft deletes wait here until restored or deleted forever. Delete forever exists only on these routes; no MCP tool can do it.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/bin` | Deleted notes and removed photos, newest deleted first: `{notes, images}`. Query: `tag` (repeatable, all must match). |
| `DELETE /api/bin/notes/:id` | Delete a note forever: its rows, its photos' originals and `cache/` folders, its files and its `files/<noteId>/` folder. 409 `not_deleted` when the note is not in the bin, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `DELETE /api/bin/images/:imageId` | Delete one removed photo forever: its row, original and `cache/<imageId>/`. 409 `not_deleted` when the photo is still in its note, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |

## Photos

Originals are stored byte for byte; `thumb`, `preview` and `display` are derived copies made on first request. Uploads are multipart with a `file` field, capped at 200 MB (413 `too_large`); 400 `file_required` / `bad_multipart`, 415 when the bytes are not a supported image. A photo whose original is on the other machine has `available: false`. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/images` | Upload one picture as a new photo note; the optional `body` field is the note text. 201 `{note, created: true}`, or 200 `{note, created: false}` with the note that already holds the same bytes. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/images` | Attach one more picture to a live note. 201 `{note, attached: true}`, or 200 `{note, attached: false}` with the note that already holds the bytes. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note. |
| `DELETE /api/images/:imageId` | Remove one photo from its note (soft, it goes to the recycle bin and keeps its position). Returns the note. 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/images/:imageId/restore` | Put a removed photo back at its old position. Returns the note. 409 `duplicate_image` with the holder's `note_id` when the same bytes are in another note now; 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId` | One photo's metadata and URLs, whatever its state (live, removed, in a deleted note). 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/original` | The original bytes, with the original file name in `Content-Disposition: inline`. Works for photos in the bin too. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/display` | What a browser can show: the original, or a full-resolution JPEG for HEIC, HEIF and TIFF. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/thumb` | The 480 px wide WebP used by the wall and the gallery. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/preview` | The JPEG with a 1568 px long edge that Claude is shown. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/original` | The original of a live note's first photo, kept for older links. Answers like the photo route; 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/display` | The display copy of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/thumb` | The thumbnail of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/preview` | The preview of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |

## Files

Any other file attached to a note, stored byte for byte under `files/<noteId>/` with a Windows-safe name. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/files` | Multipart `file`, attached to a live note. 201 `{note, attached: true, kind}`, or 200 with the note that already holds the bytes. `kind` is `image` when the bytes are a picture (stored as a photo), else `file`. 413 `too_large` over 200 MB, 400 `file_required` / `bad_multipart`, 404 `not_found`. |
| `DELETE /api/files/:fileId` | Remove one file from its note (soft). Returns the note. 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/files/:fileId/restore` | Put a removed file back at its old place. 409 `duplicate_file` with the holder's `note_id` when the bytes are in another note now; 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/files/:fileId` | One file's metadata (`name`, `mime`, `bytes`, `host`, `available`, `extraction_status`), whatever its state. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/files/:fileId/download` | The bytes, always as an attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff`, sandbox CSP), with `ETag` and 304. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |

## Open file location

The reveal routes start Windows Explorer from WSL (`explorer.exe` with a path from `wslpath -w`). They take an id, never a path, and are same-origin only. Each answers 202 `{ok: true}` as soon as Explorer has started, 404 `not_found`, 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host`, 409 `reveal_unavailable` when this daemon cannot start Explorer, or 500 `spawn_failed`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/capabilities` | `{reveal, movies_playback}`: whether "open file location" can work on this machine (Linux, WSL interop, `wslpath`, an Explorer binary), and whether Play can start VLC here. The wall hides the folder and play controls when false. |
| `POST /api/images/:imageId/reveal` | Open Explorer with the photo's original selected. |
| `POST /api/files/:fileId/reveal` | Open Explorer with the file selected. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/reveal` | Open the note's `files/<noteId>/` folder when it has files (available when at least one is on this machine), else select its first photo. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note, or one with neither. |

## Chat

The chat bar and the chat history page. Reads are open; edits, deletes and restores are same-origin only. Pasted chat images are stored under `chat-images/` and are never notes. Guide: [chat.md](../chat.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/chat` | `{message, thread_id?, reply_to?, image_ids?, note_image_ids?, project?}`: one chat turn. `message` may be empty when images come with it; at most 4 images in all. `project` (a repo) keeps a new thread to that project for good; an unknown `thread_id` starts a new thread. Answers as server-sent events: `accepted {thread_id, user_message_id}`, then `status {text}` and `delta {text}`, then `done {thread_id, user_message_id, assistant_message_id, reply_to, brain}`, or `error {error}`. The question is saved before the answer starts; the answer only when it finishes. Before the stream: 400 `invalid_reply_to` / `unknown_image`, 409 `not_on_this_machine`, 422 `unreadable_image`, 404 `reply_not_found`. This runs a real Claude agent on the owner's login. |
| `GET /api/chat/messages` | The chat timeline over all threads: `{messages, next_before}`, each page ascending. Query: `before` (the previous `next_before`), `limit`, `include_deleted=1`, `project` (only that repo's threads). 400 `invalid_cursor`. |
| `GET /api/chat/threads/:id` | One thread and its messages. Query: `include_deleted=1`. 404 `not_found`. |
| `PATCH /api/chat/messages/:id` | `{text}`: edit one of your own messages; the old text is kept as a revision. 400 `not_editable` (an answer) / `empty_text`, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `DELETE /api/chat/messages/:id` | Soft delete a message: `{deleted: [ids]}`. Query: `with_answer=1` on a question deletes its answer too. 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/chat/messages/:id/restore` | Bring a deleted message back. 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/chat/images` | Multipart `file` (and optional `source`: `wall`, the default, or `claude_code` from the notes-paste hook): store one pasted picture. 201 `{image, created: true}`, or 200 `{image, created: false}` when the same bytes are stored already. 400 `invalid_source` / `file_required`, 413 `too_large` over 50 MB, 415 `not_an_image`. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id` | One pasted image's metadata, with `available`. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/original` | The pasted image as uploaded. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/display` | The pasted image in a form a browser can show. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/thumb` | The pasted image's WebP thumbnail. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/preview` | The pasted image's JPEG preview. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |

## Capture and hooks

Called by the Claude Code hooks in `claude/hooks/`, never by the wall. Hook routes: loopback only, header `X-Notes-Capture: 1` (403 `capture_header_required`), `Content-Type: application/json` (415 `json_required`), 413 `too_large` past the body cap. A browser cannot send the header cross-origin without a preflight, which notesd never answers. Guide: [claude-code.md](../claude-code.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/capture/claude-code` | One `/n` exchange from the notes-capture hook: `{claude_session, user_uuid, prompt, answer, prompt_timestamp, answered_at, cwd?, images?}`, `images` being up to 8 `{media_type, data_base64}` of at most 20 MB each. 201 `{thread_id, user_message_id, assistant_message_id}`; 200 with `duplicate: true` when that session and prompt were captured before (nothing is written). 400 `invalid_base64`, 413 `image_too_large`, 415 `unsupported_image`. Body cap 64 MB. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/start` | From the notes-session hook (SessionStart): `{session, parent?, cwd?, name?, tmux?, host?, started_at?, source?}`. Upserts the session row (the node id is assigned on first sight). On `startup` or `clear` it links `parent` with source `env`; on `startup` in tmux with no better link it claims a pending spawn as `hook`. 200 `{session_id, node_id, parent_session_id, parent_node_id, parent_link_source, claimed}`. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/spawn` | From the notes-spawn hook (a `claude` launched by hand in tmux): `{parent, cwd, name?, host?}` records a pending spawn the child's start can claim, and prunes those older than a day. 201 `{recorded: true}`. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/link-note` | From the notes-link hook (after a notes write tool): `{session, note}` links the note to that session's node. Idempotent; the note itself never changes. 200 `{note_id, node_id, changed, made}`; 404 `unknown_session` / `not_found`; 409 `deleted`. |

## Projects and sessions

The project session graph. Rows come from the database, so they also answer for sessions copied in from another machine; transcripts and resume work only on the machine that holds the transcript (`not_on_this_machine`). A node id (`A0-3G`) is accepted in any case, with or without the dash; a malformed one answers 400 `invalid_node_id`, an unknown one 404 `not_found`. Guide: [sessions.md](../sessions.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/projects` | Repos that have Claude Code sessions, with session counts, live counts, last activity and the selected repo. |
| `GET /api/projects/selected` | `{repo}`: the repo picked in the sidebar, stored in the database. |
| `PUT /api/projects/selected` | `{repo}` (a repo or null): store the pick. 404 `unknown_repo`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/projects/:repo/sessions` | That repo's sessions for the graph: node id, parent and link source (`fork`, `env`, `hook`, `heuristic`), times, name, `live`, `host`, `available`, `unfinished`. Query: `before` (a datetime), `limit` (1 to 5000, default 2000). Sends a weak `ETag` and answers 304 to a matching `If-None-Match` (the wall polls it). 404 `unknown_repo`. |
| `GET /api/sessions/context` | Session context for the notes-prompt hook. Query: `ids` (node ids separated by commas or spaces); ids that do not exist are left out. Loopback only. |
| `GET /api/sessions/known` | Which node ids exist, with their repo: `{nodes: [{node_id, repo}]}`. Query: `ids`. The wall and the note-links mod link only these. |
| `GET /api/sessions/search` | Session search, blended like note search, with `fallback` when only words were used. Query: `q` (required), `repo`, `limit` (1 to 50, default 10). Each hit carries `via_notes` and `via_replies` like the `sessions_search` tool. |
| `GET /api/sessions/usage` | Tokens and cost per session or per month. Query: `by=node\|month` (default `month`), `repo`, `month` (`YYYY-MM`), `limit` (1 to 200, default 20). |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId` | One session in full: summary, prompts, commits, plan docs, files edited, its notes (made or linked), tokens and cost, parent and children, `host`, `available`, `context`, and `fork` for a fork. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/transcript` | Passages of the transcript. Query: `query` (words to match), `limit`. On a fork only the records after the fork point are read (`starts_at_fork_point: true`). 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for the other machine's session. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/prompts` | Every stored prompt of a session, numbered, in full. Read from the database, so it works without the transcript. `complete: false` with `incomplete_reason` (`not_backfilled`, `transcript_pruned`) when only excerpts are kept. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/context` | The session's current context: `{node_id, host, available, context}`, `context` being `{tokens, window, percent, band, model, at, window_source, peak_tokens}` or null when no main-chain reply with token usage was seen. `band` is `green` below 40 %, `amber` below 70 %, `red` from 70 %. Works without the transcript. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/context/stream` | Server-sent events: one `context` event with the same JSON on connect, another whenever this machine's ingest stores a reply that changes tokens, model or window, and heartbeats. The other machine's sessions send only the first event, so the wall polls the JSON route for those. |
| `POST /api/sessions/:nodeId/summarize` | Ask for a summary now. Records the request only; the owning machine's summary worker serves it first on its next pass. `{node_id, summary_state, summary_requested_at}`; repeating it is a no-op. 409 `empty_session` for a session with no tokens. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/sessions/:nodeId/resume` | `{prompt?, fresh?}` (unknown keys are refused, 400 `invalid_body`): open the session again in a new tmux window, or switch to it when it is live. 200 `{action, window?, cwd?, original_cwd?, job_id?, prompt_delivered?}` with `action` one of `focused`, `messaged`, `resumed`, `spawned`, `attached`. `fresh: true` writes a handoff file under `handoffs/` and starts a new session with it; a live background job gets a `claude attach <job>` window. 404 `not_on_this_machine`, 409 `no_tmux` / `live_outside_tmux`, 500 `spawn_failed`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/handoff` | Dry run of "Spawn fresh": `{node_id, tokens, window, percent, baseline, exchanges_included, exchanges_total, truncated}`, the estimated starting context of the new session. Writes no file and runs no git; works without the transcript. |

## Seer Adversarial

The read model over Seer's database plus the reviewer's switch. Reads work with `NOTESD_ADVERSARY=off`; they answer 503 `seer_unavailable` (`detail`: `not_reachable`, `not_migrated`, `query_failed`) when Seer cannot be read. A method id is accepted in any case and a twin's id means its original; 400 `invalid_id`, 404 `not_found`. Guide: [adversary.md](../adversary.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/adversary/overview` | Every method with its Claude twin and SPY: `roster`, `methods` (returns, objections, coverage, checklists), `cause`, `latest`, `last_review`, `reviewer`. |
| `GET /api/adversary/methods/:id` | One method: curves, stats, checklists, the current decision's verdict cards, every decision, the objection record, revisions, and the three-way comparison for a daily method. |
| `GET /api/adversary/methods/:id/decisions/:session` | One decision's verdict cards (`session` is a date): reason, sources, host, `late`, weight and twin weight. 400 `invalid_session`. |
| `GET /api/adversary/daily/:id` | The three-way for a daily method on one session: the ranked list with both verdicts, what each book bought, the disagreement grid. Query: `session` (default: the latest). 400 `not_bracket` for a method that is not daily. |
| `GET /api/adversary/scorecard/:id` | Each objection's return over the method's horizon against the kept picks, and, for a daily method, Claude against C on the nights they disagree. |
| `GET /api/adversary/toggle` | Whether automatic reviews are on, a switch kept in this machine's database. 503 `reviewer_off` when this daemon has no reviewer. |
| `PUT /api/adversary/toggle` | `{on}`: turn automatic reviews on or off. 503 `reviewer_off`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/adversary/review-now` | `{strategy_id?}`: start one review pass now, even while automatic reviews are off. 202 `{started, reason}` before it finishes (`reason` says when it queued behind a running pass). 503 `reviewer_off`. Same-origin only. |

## Movies

With `NOTESD_MOVIES=off` every route here answers 503 `movies_off`, except `GET /api/movies/player`, which answers `{available: false, reason: "movies_off"}`. Files, plays and VLC belong to the machine that holds them (each row names its host). Writes and anything that starts VLC are same-origin only. Guide: [movies.md](../movies.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/movies` | The library: `{titles}`, one entry per title with `poster_url` and its derived `state`. Query: `q` (full text over title and synopsis), `state`, `kind=movie\|tv`, `company`, `person`, `finished_from`, `finished_to`, `sort` (default `recent`), `limit`. |
| `GET /api/movies/stream` | The Stream side of the page: `{enabled: true, titles, fresh_days, site_titles}`, the titles with a stream source verified on this machine in the last `fresh_days` days (`NOTESD_STREAM_FRESH_DAYS`) and not marked stale, and those last played here on a streaming site (which have no source to verify), each in the same shape as `GET /api/movies`. `site_titles` are this machine's titles played on a streaming site that TMDB does not list, the one played last first: `{id, site, site_url, kind, name, year, poster_url, overview, country, status, genres, also_known, season, episode, played_at}`, with the poster and the words as the site's own page gives them and `season`, `episode` the episode last played (null for a film); they have no title page. With direct streaming off (`NOTESD_DIRECT_STREAM=off`): `{enabled: false, reason: "direct_stream_off", titles: []}`. Every title answer (`GET /api/movies/:id` and the routes that return a title) also marks each of its `stream_sources` with `fresh`, the same test. |
| `GET /api/movies/trending` | The Trending section under the Stream side's grid: `{enabled: true, titles, listed_at, status}`, this machine's daily list of the most seeded films and series on the torrent indexes (`NOTESD_TRENDING_SIZE` of each, films first, then series, each by seeds). A title is the grid's shape plus `trending: {kind_rank, seeds, index, release, size_bytes, listed_at, probe}`; `seeds` is what the index lists, `probe` is null until the swarm was opened, else `{outcome, detail, at}` with `outcome` `confirmed` (a peer sent a file list holding a video), `no_peers`, `no_video` or `error`. A title the owner has seen, started or marked not interested is read from the library at each request and left out at once, whatever the list says. `status` is the job's `{enabled, running, next_check_at, settings, last_pass}`; `last_pass.stopped` is `done`, `no_listing` (the indexes listed nothing: the old list stays), `busy` (a play cut the probes short), `no_peers_here` (the control torrent found no peer: nothing was judged), `closed` or `error`. Off: `{enabled: false, reason, titles: [], listed_at: null}` with `reason` `setting_off`, `movies_off`, `direct_stream_off`, `torrent_off` or `no_tmdb`. |
| `POST /api/movies/trending/refresh` | The Trending section's refresh icon: one pass now (a new list from the indexes, then the swarm probes). Answers 202 `{started, status}` at once, `started: false` when a pass was already running; 409 `trending_off` when the job is off. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/unmatched` | This machine's files that are not in the library: `{files}`, each with its `reason` (`too_short`, `no_match`, `low_confidence`, `tmdb_error`, `no_tmdb_credentials`, `probe_failed`). |
| `GET /api/movies/status` | Whether the library is on, its roots, the last pass with its counts, and `counts` of titles and files. |
| `GET /api/movies/search-tmdb` | TMDB search, for picking the title of an unmatched file: `{results}`. Query: `q` (required), `kind=movie\|tv`, `year`. 503 `tmdb_off` without credentials, 502 `tmdb_error`. |
| `GET /api/movies/events` | Server-sent events: `event: changed` after every pass or write that changes the library, and heartbeats. |
| `GET /api/movies/:movieId` | One title by movie id (`M-23T4`, any case). An episode's movie id answers its series. Same body as the route below. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/movies/:id` | One title by key (`movie-<tmdb id>` or `tv-<tmdb id>`): release date, synopsis, studios, crew, cast, rating, watched, review, the episode list, and every file (deleted ones too) with its `state`, `available`, season and episode. 404 `not_found`. `stream_sources`: this machine's verified stream sources of the title (direct streaming; season and episode 0 for a film): `provider`, `manifest_kind`, `best_height`, `en_subtitle`, `verified_at`, and `stale_at` when its last resolve found no source. `played_through`: how the title was last played on this machine, `{channel, provider, played_at, season, episode}` with `channel` `vlc` (a downloaded file), `cloud` (`provider` names the cloud provider), `torrent` or `site` (`provider` names the streaming site), or null when it never was; a play with no source named goes there again. `stream_failed`: `{cloud_at, torrent_at}`, when every cloud provider, and every torrent, last found nothing for the title here (null: never, or one played since). `played_methods`: what last played the title through each stream method here, newest first: `{method, provider, played_at, season, episode}` with `method` `cloud` (`provider` names the provider), `torrent` or a streaming site's name; a play that names its method goes there first. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/user` | `{watched?, not_interested?, interested?, rating?, review?}` (at least one): the watched flag, the "not interested" mark (the Stream side shows the title only under that filter, and the prober stops counting and re-checking it), the "interested" mark (the Stream side's watch list; setting one of the two marks clears the other), 0 to 5 stars or null, and the review, which is kept as a note tagged `#movie` and linked to the title. Returns the title. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/:id/story` | The stored story of a film, or of one episode (`?season=&episode=`): `{story: {season, episode, text, model, written_at, provider, cues} \| null, cached: true}`. Reads the store only; no model is called. 503 `story_off` without the stories service. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/story` | `{season?, episode?}` (a film: neither). The story of a film or an episode, with every spoiler, as the page's book icon asks for it: the stored one (`cached: true`), else its dialogue is read (the stored one, else the English subtitle of a stream source resolved out of sight), Claude writes the story from it in one call (`NOTESD_MOVIES_STORY_MODEL`), and it is kept on the dialogue, so it is written once. `{story, cached}`. 404 `not_found`; 503 `story_off` (the model is off or no claude binary) or `no_dialogue` (none stored, and direct streaming is off here); 502 `no_source` / `no_subtitle` / `resolve_failed` (the dialogue could not be read) or `story_failed` (the model call failed). Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/people/:personId` | A person by TMDB id, for the pop-up a name on a title's page opens: `{entity: {kind: "person", name, image_url, description, facts, link}, titles}`. `titles` is every film and series TMDB credits them on (talk shows, news, appearances as themselves and thanks left out), newest first, at most 120: `{kind, tmdb_id, title_id, title, year, release_date, poster_url, note, movie_id, mark, interested, has_file}`, where `note` joins their roles, `movie_id` is null for a title that is not stored, `mark` is `watched`, `started`, `not_interested` or null and `interested` the watch-list mark, both as read at this request, and `has_file` says a file is on this machine. 404 `not_found`, 503 `tmdb_off`, 502 `tmdb_error`. |
| `GET /api/movies/companies/:companyId` | A studio by TMDB id, in the same shape: its logo, TMDB's description (often empty), where it is and its parent company as `facts`, and the films and series it made up to a year ahead, newest first (two TMDB pages per kind), each marked as above. 404 `not_found`, 503 `tmdb_off`, 502 `tmdb_error`. |
| `GET /api/movies/:id/genres/:genre` | The stored guide of one genre of a title: `{guide, cached: true}` with `guide` null when none was written yet, else `{entity: {kind: "genre", name, description, ...}, titles, written_at, model}` (titles marked at this request, as for a person; `note` says what each shares with the title). Reads the store only; no model is called. 503 `guide_off` without the guides service. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/genres/:genre` | `{refresh?}` (an empty body is `{}`). What the genre means for this title, as a click on the genre asks for it: the stored guide (`cached: true`), else Claude collates one with web search in one run (`NOTESD_MOVIES_STORY_MODEL`; about a minute): a short description and up to 16 titles of that genre closest to this one in tone and premise, each then found on TMDB by name and year (one TMDB does not list is left out) and kept in `movie_genre_guides`, so it is written once per title and genre. `refresh: true` writes it again. `{guide, cached}`. 404 `not_found` / `not_a_genre`; 503 `guide_off` (the model is off, no claude binary or no TMDB credentials); 502 `guide_failed`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/ensure` | `{kind, tmdb_id}`: stores a title TMDB lists and the library does not hold yet (TMDB details, as its first stream would), so its pop-up and page can open: `{title_id, movie_id}`. An already stored title answers the same. 502 `not_stored` when TMDB does not answer for it or no credentials are configured. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/site-play` | `{site, season?, episode?}` (`site` one of `idlix`, `lk21`, `flicksy`, `dramacool`; a series needs both numbers): plays the title on that streaming site, full screen in the streaming Chrome, as the play menu's site rows do. From the page the site last played it from on this machine when one is remembered (`movie_title_methods`); else the streaming command searches the site for the title's name and year and plays it only when exactly one title matches. The play is kept, so the site is how the title plays from then on. 200 `{ok: true, site, site_url, site_play}`. 404 `no_match` / `no_episode` / `not_found`, 409 `several_matches` / `series` (a site that plays films only), 502 `not_playing`, 503 `streaming_off` / `movies_off`, 400 `no_episode` for a series without its numbers. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/:id/pahe` | The title's download pages on pahe.ink, as the `/pahe` skill's search returns them for its name and year: `{matches: [{title, url, year, release}], search_url}`, best source first; `matches` is empty when pahe lists none. 502 `pahe_error` (with `search_url` when known), 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/episodes/watched` | `{watched, season}` or `{watched, episodes: [{season, episode}]}`: mark every episode of one season of a series finished, or the listed ones, or take the marks off. A mark needs no file. `{watched, changed, title}`: `changed` lists the episodes whose mark changed, so sending them back with `watched` flipped undoes the call. 400 `not_a_series` for a film, 404 `no_episodes` for a season with none. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/watched` | `{watched}`: mark one file or episode finished, or take the mark off. `{file_id, title}`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/assign` | `{kind, tmdb_id, season?, episode?}` (season and episode together, `tv` only): put an unmatched or wrongly matched file under that TMDB title. 503 `tmdb_off`, 502 `tmdb_error`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/sync` | Start a library pass now: 202 `{started: true, report: null}`. Query: `wait=true` answers 200 with the pass report when it ends. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/player` | `{available, reason, current, stream, starting, busy}`: whether playback works on this machine, the VLC play notesd is following now (`current`), and the stream on screen in the player page (`stream`: `{session_id, title_id, season, episode, provider, state, position, duration, last_report_at}` with `state` `playing` or `paused`); each null when there is none. A stream leaves 20 s after its page last reported. `starting` lists the stream plays being started (`{kind, tmdb_id, season, episode, title, provider, since, stage}`): asked for and still resolving (a cloud resolve, a torrent's indexes and swarms), or opened less than 30 s ago with a page that does not report yet. `busy` is true when any of the three is there: the one thing to read before restarting the daemon (`scripts/install.sh` does). |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/play` | Start VLC on the file at its resume point (the last position; the start when there is none or it was finished). 202 `{ok: true, play}`. When the file is already open in the VLC notesd follows, no second VLC starts: that window comes to the front, plays if it was paused, and `play.already_playing` is true. 404 `not_found` / `not_on_this_machine`, 410 `file_missing`, 409 `player_unavailable` with `reason`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/site-play` | `{site, url, name?, original_name?, year?, kind?, season?, episode?}` from the streaming command (`claude/streaming/cli.mjs`, which the site skills and the streaming tools run) after a site's player started: `url` is the title's page on the site as its search returned it, `kind` `movie` or `series`, `season` and `episode` the site's numbers. The title is found by its name and year (stored titles first, then TMDB; a one-episode "series" no series matches is looked up as a film), stored when it is new, and gets one closed `movie_plays` row (source `stream`, the site as `provider`, position unknown) and the site as the channel it is streamed through from then on, which also lists it on the Stream side. 200 `{recorded: true, title_id, season, episode}`; when no stored or TMDB title carries the name and year, the title is kept by what the site says of it instead (the command is asked for the page's details) and the answer is `{recorded: true, title_id: null, site_title_id, season, episode}`; or `{recorded: false, reason}` with `reason` `no_name`, `no_match`, `several_matches` (with `candidates`), `tmdb_unavailable` or `not_stored`: the play happened, it is only not kept. Loopback only, and only with the `x-notes-site-play` header: 403 `forbidden`. 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`, 503 `movies_off`. |
| `POST /api/movies/site-titles/:id/play` | `{episode?, season?}` (an empty body is `{}`): plays a title TMDB does not list (`site_titles` of `GET /api/movies/stream`) on its streaming site again, full screen in the streaming Chrome: the film, or the episode named, else the one after the last played. 200 `{ok: true, site, site_url, season, episode, site_play}`, and the row then holds that episode. 404 `no_episode` when the site lists no such episode (the row keeps the one it had), 502 `not_playing` with the command's `play` when the player did not start, 404 `not_found` (also for another machine's title), 503 `streaming_off` / `movies_off`, 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `DELETE /api/movies/site-titles/:id` | Takes a title TMDB does not list off this machine's Stream side. 200 `{ok: true}`, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/continue` | `{title?}`: what the `movies_continue` tool does: resume the latest unfinished episode or film, else start the next episode that is here (`action` `already_playing` when that file is already open in the followed VLC). Without `title`, the title of the newest play. Same errors as play; 400 `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/player/health` | This machine's VLC health log: the newest samples, per-VLC run summaries, hang lines, video stalls (`stalls`), display-driver resets seen while VLC ran (`gpu_resets`) and crash incidents. Query: `limit` (samples, 1 to 2000, default 200; 400 `invalid_limit`). 503 `movies_off` without a monitor. |

## Direct streaming

With `NOTESD_DIRECT_STREAM=off`, `NOTESD_MOVIES=off`, or no direct-stream service, every route here answers 503 `direct_stream_off` before any other check. A session lives in this daemon's memory only: its id is 32 random characters, it ends 4 hours after its last request or 24 hours after it began, and a restart ends it; an unknown or ended one answers 403 `unknown_session`. Guide: [streaming.md](../streaming.md#direct-streaming).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/stream/play` | `{kind, tmdb_id, season?, episode?, resume_s?, provider?}` (`season` and `episode` together, `tv` only; `provider` asks that one provider only and passes over a cache): resolve the title through the provider registry (without `provider`, what streamed the title last time on this machine is asked first: that cloud provider alone, the others only when it has no stream now; the torrents when a torrent streamed it, or when the title never streamed and its cloud search found nothing in the last three days; and a title last played on a streaming site plays there again, answering 200 `{ok: true, site, site_url, site_play}` with no session, or goes on as usual when the site does not start it), record each provider's health on this machine, then open the player page full screen in the streaming Chrome. When this machine has a cache of the title (`ready` or `downloading`, made for its original language), the play comes from it and nothing is resolved: `attempts` is `[]` and `session.cached` names the cache. A failed cache, or one made on the other machine, is passed over. 200 `{ok: true, page_url, session, attempts}` with `session` as the route below. 502 `no_source` with every provider's `attempts`; 502 `resolve_failed` with `reason` (`no_chrome`, `chrome_not_reachable`, `script_failed`, ...); 502 `open_failed` with `session_id` and `page_url`. `provider: "torrent"` (any case) asks only the torrent source (a finished download of the title on this machine first, with no index and no swarm; else a torrent found by the title's IMDb id and played from the swarm). Without a provider, a finished torrent download on this machine comes right after the stream cache, and when no provider resolves the title (or the resolve cannot run) the torrent source is tried before answering: `attempts` then go on with `Index: <name>` per torrent index asked and `Torrent: <release>` per torrent tried (`resolved`, `no_stream`, `dubbed`, `unplayable`, `error`). A torrent session has `provider` `Torrent` and `session.torrent` set. 503 `torrent_off` when `provider` is `torrent` and torrents are off (`NOTESD_TORRENT=off`). 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id` | What the player page needs: `{session_id, kind, tmdb_id, season, episode, title, provider, manifest_kind, manifest_url, subtitles, best_height, audio_lang, audio, resume_s, prev_episode, next_episode, created_at, refreshed_at, expires_at, cached, torrent, subtitle_rev}`. `subtitle_rev` counts the times the session's `subtitles` changed after the play started (Wyzie Synced re-timed a subtitle from outside the stream, or a cloud stream's outside subtitle arrived late); the page loads them again when the number in a position report's answer differs. A cloud session whose source has no English subtitle carries the title's outside one (`GET /api/stream/subs/:title/:name`), asked for when the session is first read, for at most 4 s. `prev_episode` and `next_episode` are `{season, episode}` or null: a series' neighbouring episodes, for the player's buttons. `audio_lang` is the title's original language and `audio` what the resolve heard in the stream (`{languages, tracks, original, track}`; `track` is the manifest's audio track in the original language, which the player selects). `manifest_url` and each subtitle `url` are pass-through addresses on this daemon; an `.srt` track is served as WebVTT, and each track says whether it is `english`. A track with `growing: true` (and `format: "cues"`) is a cue feed (`GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/cues/:track`): its `url` answers JSON cues, read again until the feed is complete. `cached` is `{id, state, height}` when the session plays from this machine's stream cache (`state` `ready` or `downloading`), else null; then `manifest_url` and each subtitle `url` are the cache's file route (`/api/stream/cache/<id>/f/...`), not pass-through addresses. `torrent` is `{info_hash, file_index, name, index, state, seeds}` when the session plays from a torrent (`state` `ready` once the file is whole on this machine, else `downloading`; `index` and `seeds` null for a replay from disk), else null; then `manifest_url` is the torrent's file route (`/api/stream/torrent/<hash>/f/<index>`). Reading a torrent session whose page had closed takes its torrent again. 403 `unknown_session`. |
| `GET /api/stream/subs/:title/:name` | One WebVTT file of a title's English subtitle from outside its stream, kept on this machine for cloud streams that have none: `:title` is `movie-<tmdb id>` or `tv-<tmdb id>-s<season>e<episode>`, `:name` `outside.vtt` (as a subtitle service gave it) or `synced.vtt` (re-timed by Wyzie Synced). 404 `not_found` for anything else, and on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id/p` | The pass-through. Query: `u` (the stream host address), `vtt=1` (hand a subtitle file back as WebVTT). Fetches `u` with only the `Referer`, `Origin` and `User-Agent` the resolve captured and the player's `Range`, and streams the answer back with the host's status, also in `X-Notesd-Upstream`. HLS playlists and DASH manifests come back with every address rewritten to this route. 403 `unknown_session`; 403 `forbidden_host`, and nothing is fetched, when `u` is not on a host the session's resolve returned or that a playlist, manifest or redirect fetched through the session named. 502 `upstream_error`. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/refresh` | Resolve the session's title again (a token expired) and keep the same session id and page: returns the session like the route above. 502 `no_source` / `resolve_failed` leave the session as it was. A session that plays from a cache reads the cache again: while it can still be played the session keeps it and nothing is resolved; once it is gone or failed the title is resolved and the session goes on through the pass-through. A torrent session keeps its torrent, taking it again when it was let go; 502 `resolve_failed` with `reason` `torrent_gone` when the swarm cannot open it. 403 `unknown_session`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/source` | From the player page when the film keeps stalling (three stalls within two minutes): resolve the session's title again without the provider it plays from, or any it left before, and move the session to the provider that answers, under the same id. 200 with the session like `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id` plus `switched`, `reason` and `from` (the provider it was on). `switched: false` leaves the session as it was: `reason` `no_other_source` (no other provider answered; the title is not marked stale) or `cached` (it plays from the stream cache). A later refresh never goes back to a provider the session left. A torrent session moves to the next torrent the indexes listed (no index is asked again) and lets go of the old one; `from` is `Torrent: <release>`. 403 `unknown_session`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/cache` | `{start?}` from the player page after a pause that lasted 2 s: with `start: true` the session's title starts downloading to this machine's stream cache (marked `auto`; a failed one carries on), without it the call only looks. Once the cache knows its source, the session moves onto it under the same id, in the title's original language only. 200 with the session like `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id` plus `moved` (this call moved it: the page loads the cache's manifest at its position) and `cache` (`{id, state, error, progress}`; null when this daemon caches nothing). The page asks again every 4 s until `moved` or `state: "failed"`, and while it plays a cache that still downloads. A torrent session is never cached (`moved: false`, `cache: null`). 403 `unknown_session`, 400 `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/episode` | `{to: "prev" \| "next"}` from the player page's previous and next episode buttons: resolves the episode before or after the session's (TMDB's order, specials left out; never an episode that has not aired) and returns a new session for it, in the shape of `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id`. The page then plays that session without leaving full screen. 404 `no_episode` (a film, or no episode on that side), 502 `no_source` / `resolve_failed` (the page keeps playing what it has), 403 `unknown_session`, 400 `invalid_body`. A neighbour with a cache on this machine plays from it, as `POST /api/stream/play` does. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/position` | `{position_s, duration_s?, ended?, paused?, beat?, closed?}` from the player page, every 5 s while it is open, on pause, on play, at the end and as it closes: written on the one open `movie_plays` row (source `stream`) of this session, which the first report opens and `ended: true` closes; opening one closes this machine's other open stream play. The title's watch state derives from it as from a VLC play. Each report also makes the session the stream on screen (`GET /api/movies/player`), `playing` or `paused`, until `ended` or `closed`; a `beat` (a paused page saying it is still open) for the stream already on screen writes nothing and answers `play_id: null`. A `closed` or `ended` report also makes a torrent session let go of its torrent (the daemon leaves the swarm once nothing else uses it). 200 `{ok: true, play_id, ended, subtitle_rev}`; `subtitle_rev` is the session's now (see `GET /api/stream/sessions/:id`). 400 `invalid_body`, 404 `unknown_session` / `unknown_title` (the title is not stored and TMDB cannot give it: the play is not recorded; the page ignores it), 503 `direct_stream_off`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/report` | `{page?: {stage, error, errors, log, title?, position_s?}}` from the player page's report button (the page's own view of the failure; every address in it loses its query): writes the evidence snapshot of the session at once, then opens a new window in the most recently attached tmux session running Claude Code (`--permission-mode auto`) in the mcp-notes checkout on `/report-stream-bug <folder>`, named `stream-bug-<first 6 characters of the id>`. 200 `{ok: true, dir, window, complete}` (`complete: false` when the daemon no longer knows the session and the page's log stands in for it). One report per session, remembered by `report.json` in the folder across restarts: 409 `already_reported` `{dir}`. When the window cannot open the snapshot is kept: 409 `no_tmux` `{dir, complete}`, 500 `spawn_failed` `{dir, message, complete}`; a later call opens it on the same folder. 403 `unknown_session` (a malformed id, or an ended session sent with no `page`), 500 `snapshot_failed`, 503 `report_off`, 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/sessions/:id/events` | `{lines: [{text, at?, stage?, position_s?, buffer_s?}]}` (1 to 50 lines, `text` up to 2000 characters) from the player page: its log lines as it writes them (refreshes, recoveries, errors, subtitle failures), with the position and the seconds buffered ahead, appended to this machine's stream evidence log under the session id. Any address in a line keeps only its host and path. The session need not be live. 200 `{ok: true, recorded}`. 400 `invalid_session` (not a session id), `invalid_json`, `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/evidence/snapshot` | `{session_id?}` (an empty body is `{}`): writes a new folder `<data dir>/movies/stream-reports/<UTC stamp>-<first 6 characters of the id>/` on this machine holding `session.json` (the live session's source: provider, attempts, hosts, refreshes, addresses as host and path, captured header names only), `evidence.jsonl` (its pass-through and session records) and `player.json` (the page's posted lines). Without `session_id`: the stream on screen, else the session of the newest record. 200 `{ok: true, dir, session_id, complete, records, player_lines}`; `complete` is false when the session has ended (only its log records are left) or there is none. 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`, 500 `snapshot_failed`. Same-origin only: a script sends an `Origin` equal to the address it calls. |
| `GET /api/stream/evidence` | This machine's stream evidence log, oldest first: `{host, file, records}`. A `request` record is one pass-through answer: `stream_host`, `path` (never the query), `range`, `kind`, `status` (the stream host's; null when it never answered), `answer` (what the player got), `ttfb_ms`, `bytes`, `duration_ms`, `kbps`, `redirects`, `outcome` (`end`, `aborted`, `error`, `refused`) and `error`. A `player` record is a posted page line; a `session` record is a session `created`, `refreshed`, `refresh_failed`, `switched` (moved to another provider) or `cached` (moved onto this machine's cache). Query: `session` (a session id), `limit` (1 to 2000, default 200). 400 `invalid_session` / `invalid_limit`. Reads only. |
| `GET /api/stream/prober` | The background prober of this machine: `{enabled, off_reason, host, running, next_pass_at, settings, catalog: {size, fresh}, last_pass}`. `off_reason` says why it does not run: `setting_off` (the default), `movies_off`, `direct_stream_off`, `no_tmdb`, or `not_linux` / `no_interop` / `no_powershell` when the Windows idle time cannot be read. `last_pass` counts re-checks, probes and failures, and `stopped` says why the pass ended (`not_idle`, `busy`, `probe_budget`, `time_budget`, `catalog_full`, `no_candidates`, `chrome_unavailable`, `error`, `closed`). Starts nothing. 503 `direct_stream_off` without direct streaming. |
| `POST /api/stream/prober/pass` | The owner asks for one prober pass now (the Stream side's refresh button). The pass rebuilds the candidate listing whatever its age and does not wait for the laptop to be idle; the budget holds and nothing is probed while something plays. Answers 202 at once with the prober's state (`running: true`), also when a pass was already running; 409 `prober_off` with the state when the prober is off. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/cache` | `{kind, tmdb_id, season?, episode?, max_height?}` (`season` and `episode` together, `tv` only; `max_height` 100 to 4320): cache the film or episode on this machine. Answers at once; the download runs in the daemon, one at a time (the rest wait, `queued`): the title is resolved like a play, out of sight, then one HLS rendition (the tallest, or the tallest not above `max_height`) with the audio rendition in the title's original language, its segments, init sections and AES-128 keys, and the English subtitle as WebVTT, or a plain file by byte ranges, go to `<NOTESD_STREAM_CACHE_DIR>/<id>/`. A segment that fails is tried six times with backoff; a refused token (401/403/410) resolves the title again and the download carries on by segment index. 202 `{ok: true, started: true, cache}` when a download was queued (a failed cache starts again from what is on disk); 200 `{ok: true, started: false, cache}` when it is ready or already downloading; 409 `cache_exists` with `cache` when this machine holds the title at another `max_height` (clear it first); 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/stream/cache` | Every cache in the database, newest first: `{host, caches}`. A cache is `{id, kind, tmdb_id, season, episode, host, available, state (downloading, ready, failed), running, queued, provider, manifest_kind, height, max_height, audio_lang, subtitle, segments_total, segments_done, progress, bytes, duration_s, resolves, error, error_detail, auto, playlist_url, subtitle_url, created_at, updated_at, completed_at}`. `auto` marks a cache a pause in the player started: it clears itself three days after it was last written. `available` is false for the other machine's cache, whose `playlist_url` and `subtitle_url` are null. `error` on a failed one: `cache_unsupported` (DASH, DRM, a live stream, a file without byte ranges), `no_source`, `resolve_failed`, `download_failed`, `token_refused`, `source_changed`, `disk_error`. |
| `GET /api/stream/cache/:id` | One cache, in the shape above, with the running download's live progress. 404 `unknown_cache`. |
| `GET /api/stream/cache/:id/map` | What of a cache is on this machine's disk, for the player's timeline: `{duration_s, ranges}` with `ranges` the stretches in seconds, `[from, to]`, in order. HLS: the video segments whose files exist; a plain file: the whole title once it is ready. 404 `unknown_cache` (also for the other machine's cache). |
| `DELETE /api/stream/cache/:id` | Clear a cache of this machine: its download stops, its folder is deleted and its row removed, so no listing shows it. `{ok: true, id}`. 404 `unknown_cache`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for the other machine's cache, which stays. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/stream/cache/:id/f/:name` | A file of a cache, from this machine's disk, with `Range` (206, 416): `master.m3u8`, `video.m3u8`, `audio.m3u8`, `v-init-<k>.mp4`, `v-key-<k>.key`, `v-00001.ts` (or `.m4s`, `.aac`; `a-` for the audio rendition), `subtitle.vtt`, `video.mp4`. The playlists name every segment from the start, so a player can seek anywhere while the cache downloads; a file not on disk yet is fetched from the stream host at once, ahead of the queue, and stored (a plain file chunk by chunk). 404 `unknown_cache`, 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `cache_failed`, 502 `upstream_error`. |
| `POST /api/stream/cache/:id/play` | `{resume_s?}` (the body may be empty): play one stream cache by its id, as `POST /api/stream/play` plays a title from its cache: the player page opens full screen in the streaming Chrome and nothing is resolved. 200 `{ok: true, page_url, session, attempts: []}` with `session.cached` naming the cache. 404 `unknown_cache`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for a cache made on the other machine; 409 `cache_failed` (its download failed); 409 `cache_language` (it was made for another language than the title's original); 502 `open_failed`. 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |

## Torrents

Torrent downloads of this machine: a film's video and subtitle files from a swarm, served from this daemon. Every route answers 503 `direct_stream_off` without direct streaming and 503 `torrent_off` with `NOTESD_TORRENT=off`. A download belongs to the machine that made it: the other machine sees it with `available: false`, and its file routes answer 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host`. Speeds are in kilobits per second. Guide: [streaming.md](../streaming.md#torrents).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent` | This machine's torrent engine and every download in the database: `{host, port, upload_cap_bytes_per_s, keep_days, discovery, swarm, downloads}`. `port` is the engine's listening port, null while no torrent is in the swarm (the engine starts with the first torrent and stops after the last). `swarm` is the torrents in the swarm now, `{info_hash, name, users, peers, down_kbps, up_kbps}`; `downloads` are in the shape of `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash`, newest first. Starts nothing. |
| `POST /api/stream/torrent` | `{info_hash, kind, tmdb_id, season?, episode?, name?, trackers?, files?}` (`name`: the release name as an index lists it): open a torrent for a title and answer its file list once a peer sends it (60 s at most): `{ok: true, from_disk, files: [{index, path, length, media}], torrent}`, `media` `video`, `subtitle` or null. Nothing is downloaded until `files` names the indexes to use, which must be video or subtitle files; those are downloaded in order under `<NOTESD_TORRENT_DIR>/<info hash>/`, and this route holds the torrent in the swarm until `POST .../release`. A download finished on this machine for the same title opens from disk (`from_disk: true`, its chosen files only) and joins no swarm. 400 `invalid_json` / `invalid_body` / `not_media`; 504 `no_metadata` (no peer sent the file list); 422 `unsafe_path` (a file would land outside the torrent's folder); 502 `engine_error`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/stream/torrent/:hash/release` | Let go of the torrent `POST /api/stream/torrent` holds: `{ok: true, released, torrent}` (`released: false` when it held nothing). A finished download leaves the swarm at once, an unfinished one three minutes after its last file request. 404 `unknown_torrent`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash` | One download: `{info_hash, host, available, kind, tmdb_id, season, episode, name, release, state (downloading, ready, failed), error, file_index, file_length, files, bytes_done, progress, duration_s, in_swarm, users, peers, down_kbps, up_kbps, file_url, created_at, updated_at, completed_at, played_at}`. `files` are the chosen files and `file_index` the video; `peers` and the speeds are live while it is in the swarm, else 0. `file_url` is null on the other machine. `error` on a failed one: `no_metadata`, `unsafe_path`, `engine_error`. 404 `unknown_torrent`. |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/map` | What of the video is on this machine's disk: `{duration_s, ranges, length, byte_ranges}`. `byte_ranges` are `[from, to)` byte stretches in order; `ranges` the same in seconds by proportion once a duration is known, empty before. For a torrent whose file plays as a remux, `ranges` is the remuxed stretch from 0 and `duration_s` the film's length from the probe. 404 `unknown_torrent` (also for the other machine's download). |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/cues/:track` | A growing subtitle of a torrent session (`track` is `embedded-<file index>-<stream index>`, the English text track inside the file, or `whisper-<file index>`): `{cues: [{start_s, end_s, text}], next, complete}`, the cues after the first `after` (query, default 0, at most 2000 per answer). `text` is WebVTT cue text. The player reads it again from `next` every 4 s until `complete`. Kept on this machine's disk beside the torrent, so a replay has it at once. 404 `unknown_feed`; 400 `invalid_query`; 503 `torrent_off`. |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/f/:index` | A chosen file of a download, with `Range` (206, 416): from disk once it is whole, else from the swarm, which fetches the pieces of the asked range before the rest of the file. Only the video and subtitle files chosen for it are served, as video or text, never run. 404 `unknown_torrent`, 404 `not_selected`, 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host`, 409 `not_in_swarm` (unfinished and not open: play it again), 503 `closing`. |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/hls/:index/:name` | A file of the ffmpeg remux of a torrent's file `:index` that Chrome cannot play as is (an MKV, AC3, E-AC3 or DTS sound, HEVC video), from this machine's disk: `index.m3u8`, an HLS EVENT playlist that grows while the file downloads and carries `EXT-X-ENDLIST` only once ffmpeg has read the whole file and exited cleanly; `init.mp4`; `seg-00000.m4s` and on (fMP4, about 6 s each: the video copied, the original-language audio as AAC stereo), with `Range` (206, 416). The playlist is never cached. A remux session's `manifest_url` names the playlist with `remux=1` and `total_s` (the film's length), which the player reads. 404 `not_found` (no such remux or file here; only those three kinds of name are served), 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for a torrent downloaded on the other machine, 404 `remux_off` with `NOTESD_TORRENT_REMUX=off`, 503 `torrent_off`. |
| `GET /api/stream/torrent/:hash/sub/:name` | A subtitle file of a torrent on this machine, as WebVTT, with `Range` (206, 416): `file-<index>.vtt` (a subtitle file inside the torrent: SubRip converted, ASS/SSA converted with ffmpeg), `service-wyzie-<id>.vtt` or `service-<id>.vtt` (from a subtitle service: Wyzie Subs with `WYZIE_API_KEY`, else the add-on at `NOTESD_TORRENT_SUBTITLE_URL`) or `borrow.vtt` (a cloud provider's English subtitle). They are kept under `<NOTESD_TORRENT_DIR>/<hash>/.notesd-subs/`, so a replay from disk has them, and a torrent session's `subtitles` point here. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for a torrent the other machine downloaded; 503 when torrents are off. |

## Debug

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/debug/egress` | Rows and approximate bytes returned per query shape since the daemon started, largest first, plus the Neon quota breaker (`quota.tripped`, `quota.resumes_at`). `{enabled: false}` with `NOTESD_EGRESS_METER=off`. Loopback only. See [architecture.md](../architecture.md#neon). |
